items.title: How does mismatching your response to the incident's severity cost you reputation?
items.description: Picture the same credit-stealing incident, held fixed, while you vary how intensely you respond to it — from saying nothing at all, up through a calibrated private conversation, to a maximal public blowup. Drag the slider across the full range of response intensity and watch the reputational cost curve: both extremes carry a real cost (silence signals the behavior is safe to repeat; a blowup makes you look disproportionate), and the calibrated middle is where that cost bottoms out.

params.name: responseIntensity
params.label: Response intensity (0 = total silence, 100 = public blowup)

items.compute: const calibratedPoint = 35; const distance = Math.abs(params.responseIntensity - calibratedPoint); const cost = Math.round(Math.min(100, (distance / 65) * 100 * 1.0)); return { reputationalCost: cost };

items.title: How does the strength of the pattern change where you should start on the escalation ladder?
items.description: Dana starts at a private, direct conversation (rung 2) for a first-time, ambiguous incident, and only reaches a manager (rung 4) once that conversation demonstrably failed to hold. Drag the slider to represent how strong the evidence of a real, repeated pattern is — from a single ambiguous incident to a confirmed, repeated pattern with no surviving innocent explanation — and see which rung of the escalation ladder that evidence level justifies starting on.

params.name: patternStrength
params.label: Pattern strength (0 = single ambiguous incident, 100 = confirmed repeated pattern)

items.compute: let rung; if (params.patternStrength < 10) rung = 1; else if (params.patternStrength < 45) rung = 2; else if (params.patternStrength < 65) rung = 3; else if (params.patternStrength < 85) rung = 4; else rung = 5; return { startingRung: rung };

outputs.label: Escalation ladder rung to start at (1-5)
